proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, 10^n is congruent to 10^(n mod 8) modulo 13.

argument.text: At n = 0 both sides equal 1 modulo 13.
The residue 10 has order 8 modulo 13: for every n in [0, 32], 10^(n+8) is congruent to 10^n modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6.
Every integer n in [1, 40] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
For every n in [0, 40]: if 8 divides n then 10^n is congruent to 1 modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
Every n in [0, 40] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 8.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 40].
